question: Should experimental grouped Claw updates adopt this exact `--yes --plan-integrity` consent model and explicit non-transactional `update_partial` recovery contract across packages, MCP, cron, workspace, config, and provenance?
rationale: The code can enforce a chosen contract, but automation cannot decide whether OpenClaw should support a broad mutation workflow that may retain external installer or scheduler state after failure; that is an RFC-level product and operator-safety choice.

options.title: Hold for RFC and live proof
options.body: Keep the PR open and unmerged until the stack contract is accepted and live package, Gateway cron, and retained-state recovery evidence is attached.

options.title: Narrow the first apply slice
options.body: Land only owners with fully demonstrated transactional or compensating behavior and defer package and Gateway cron mutation to separately proven follow-ups.

options.title: Pause grouped mutation
options.body: Keep read-only planning but pause or close the apply stage if maintainers do not want to own partial external-state recovery as a product contract.

recommendation.title: Hold for RFC and live proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open and unmerged until the stack contract is accepted and live package, Gateway cron, and retained-state recovery evidence is attached.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main routing signal is the merged plugin/MCP lifecycle work that this PR explicitly aligns with, and the unresolved choice spans product, CLI, plugin, and operator behavior.
